newsitem.title: USA: Asarco sees copper use topping production.
newsitem.headline: Asarco sees copper use topping production.

text.p: Asarco Inc said Thursday it expects world copper consumption to continue to exceed production for at least three years.

With copper inventories remaining at historically low levels, the company continued, "We expect market fundamentals to remain favorable for copper, and with our operations performing well, Asarco should realize the benefits."

The company reported second quarter earnings including gains on the sale of investments of $51.9 million, or $1.21 per share, compared with net earnings of $72.4 million, or $1.70 per common share, for the year earlier quarter.
"Exclusive of gains from the sale of investments, the company's earnings increased by $5.1 million or 15 percent in the second quarter" compared with 1996, Chairman Richard Osborne said.

"Higher earnings in our North American copper operations resulted from increased sales volumes and gains from the company's price protection program, while our Peruvian copper operations benefited from higher copper prices and a lower tax rate. Earnings from our Peruvian copper operations had been negatively affected in the second quarter of last year by $4.1 million of adjustments to provisionally priced sales.
"Second quarter 1997 earnings also reflect improved results from the company's specialty chemicals and aggregates businesses, and the receipt of a dividend from Grupo Mexico SA," Osborne noted.
During June Asarco sold 43.4 million shares of Grupo Mexico for gross proceeds of $126.2 million, realizing an after-tax gain of $13.4 million.

Following the sales, Asarco said, it held a 17.3 percent interest in Grupo Mexico. At current market prices, the value of the company's remaining interest in Grupo Mexico is about $290 million, it continued.
In late June, Asarco announced it would use $100 million of the proceeds from the sale of Grupo Mexico shares to repurchase its own shares.
Through July 23, the company said, it had used $22.8 million to purchase about 715,000 of its shares.

Asarco said its beneficial interest in mined copper production in the second quarter of 1997 was 230 million pounds compared with 258 million pounds in the year earlier period. The principal reasons for the decrease were lower ore grades at its North American copper operations and the partial curtailment of the Hayden concentrator at Arizona's Ray mine.
The Hayden concentrator resumed full operations in May.
As of June 30, Asarco said, its lead refinery in Omaha, Neb., ceased operations.

As a result of the closure, the portion of the company's last in-first out (LIFO) metal inventory attributable to Omaha, which for financial purposes was carried at low historical values, was permanently liquidated. Also during the second quarter of 1997, the company recognized costs in its custom lead business, which included the Omaha refinery, for metals which will not be recovered.
The net effect of these events on second quarter results was not material, Asarco said.

It said the average price for copper on the New York Commodity Exchange (COMEX) in the second quarter was $1.14 per pound compared with $1.16 in the second quarter of 1996. The average London Metal Exchange (LME) copper price was also $1.14 in the second quarter of 1997 compared with $1.12 in the year-earlier period.
About 60 percent of Asarco's second quarter copper sales were based on the LME price with the balance based on COMEX quotations.
